chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“Whoever washes a dead person, let him perform ghusl.”
He said: “And if he touches him while he is still warm, then no ghusl is upon him; but when he has become cold and then he touches him, let him perform ghusl.”
I said: “Then what about one who places him into the grave?” He said: “There is no ghusl upon him; he is only touching the clothes.”
ai.seo_question: When is ghusl required after washing or touching a dead body in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ghusl after handling a deceased person. It states that ghusl is required for one who washes the dead, and also for one who touches the corpse after it has become cold, but not while it is still warm nor for one who only handles the clothed body during burial.
